$comment: D-FFI-DUPLICATE-SYMBOL-ACROSS-DESCRIPTORS-SILENTLY-ORDER-RESOLVED (P42): the RUNTIME witness for the LEGITIMATE half of CROSS-DESCRIPTOR REALIZATION AGREEMENT. <memory.h> mirrors <string.h>'s mem* surface by design, so a TU including BOTH resolves two descriptors declaring memcpy/memmove/memset/memcmp/memchr for the SAME object format -- the exact shape the agreement check compares, and the shape sqlite's shell.c really has (<string.h> at :166, <memory.h> at :7121). The sibling example shipped_memory_h includes ONLY the alias and therefore resolves ONE descriptor, so nothing in the corpus put the two side by side before this. WHAT IT PINS THAT A UNIT TEST CANNOT: that the check does not REFUSE the shipped configuration, and that the surviving import still WORKS, on every leg, at runtime. A checker that degenerated into 'duplicates are forbidden' fails this at BUILD time on all four targets. Both surfaces are used so a wrong winner is visible in the EXIT CODE, not only in the import table: the mem* five come from both descriptors, strlen/strcmp/strchr from string.json alone. exit = strlen("dss-p42") + 35 = 7 + 35 = 42. UNGATED, all 4 targets -- both headers exist on every platform (glibc/Darwin forwarders, the MSVC CRT alias), and pe must resolve them too since shell.c's include is unconditional.

optimizedPipelines.label: full-release-like
optimizedPipelines.$commentByteIdentical: Deliberately NOT given "mustDifferFromBaseline", for the SAME measured reason as the sibling shipped_memory_h: every step this example pins happens behind an EXTERN call the pipeline cannot see through (memcpy/memcmp/memchr/memset/memmove/strcmp/strchr/strlen are all imports), so no pass has a body to transform on this side of the call and the optimized image is byte-identical to the baseline. Where the image is identical the arm's exit-code/stdout comparison is x==x and cannot fail -- an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in. The arm still earns its place: it proves the AGREEMENT CHECK runs and passes on the optimized build path too, which is a different compile of the same descriptors.

optimizedPipelines.label: release
optimizedPipelines.$commentByteIdentical: Same reasoning as the arm above -- the whole body is extern calls, so the release pipeline has nothing to transform here and the image matches the baseline. Kept because the bar requires a release arm and because it re-runs descriptor resolution, which is what this example exists to exercise.
